session_read: Sunday 2026-08-16. Nothing traded since Friday's close, so every price here is Saturday's price. What changed is the evidence, and it points one way. CXMT is now projected to end 2026 within 25k wafer-starts of Micron's DRAM capacity, share at 8% against 3% a year ago -- against 15.53% of equity. The counter-scale is real and stated: wafer starts are not bits, and node density and yield still trail. The thesis desk did the right thing with it, holding MU, DRAM and SKHY at WATCH on COMPETITIVE grounds while explicitly refusing to call it a pricing verdict -- HBM3E is flat within basis, and the HBM4 'increase' is a splice artifact the tracker already flagged. Zero thesis status changes across 35 names. The book's own position is the uncomfortable part: EXTREME GREED at 82.9, NDX RSI 73, ten names over their ATR caps, aggregate risk 14.4% against a 10% ceiling, and $12.25 of cash against a 5-15% band, into NVDA's print on 08-26 at 7.72% weight. Six trims to fix exactly that have been open and unactioned. Four new proposals this run, and notably only one is an ATR trim: a cap-INDEPENDENT BX profit-take paired with a QCOM laggard buy that funds itself, an SNDK trim on the book's largest percentage gainer, and an MRVL stop raised to cost basis because the existing stop sat below it. The scorecard says 14.3% on seven graded -- a small sample, and not a flattering one.
